clue.text: What cook provided for both beverage and food

parts.note: tea is the classic British beverage
cake is a common item of food

explanation.surface: A cook lays on something to drink and something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for both' tells you the answer covers the drink and the food at once. A TEACAKE is a sweet, fruited bun, toasted and buttered in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, sweet bun is just the sort of thing a cook might bake and serve.

clue.text: Manservant returns by four to Jaffa

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the word is written in reverse

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's manservant
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A valet comes back with four oranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns VALET into TELAV. Jaffa (Yafo) is the old port now joined with Tel Aviv, and also a variety of orange.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient port of Jaffa is merged with the Israeli city into one municipality, Tel Aviv-Yafo.

clue.text: Deposed member caught in crooked deal

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside the other
crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A dethroned ruler's limb gets trapped in a corrupt deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges DEAL to ALED, and LEG is 'caught in' it. 'Deposed' here means stated under oath, not removed from power.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given in a sworn statement has been claimed but not proved.

clue.text: To be of assistance in travail

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the following word

explanation.surface: Being helpful during hard toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To help or serve a purpose is to be of use.

clue.text: Death can now be seen to be the purpose

parts.note: end means death, as in meeting one's end
in view means visible

explanation.surface: Death is now visible as the final goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an aim in sight means having a goal one is working towards.

clue.text: Airborne soldier has a favourite place for suicidal jump

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by air
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A paratrooper picks a spot to leap from to his death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties the paratrooper to a jump, but PARA is only the first piece and the jump belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall along a roof or bridge is where a despairing person might leap from.

clue.text: Blower producing 100% acidity

parts.note: pH is the measure of acidity
the whole of something, one hundred per cent, is one

explanation.surface: A wind instrument produces total sourness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blower' is British slang for the telephone. pH 1 is extremely acidic.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang calls the telephone the instrument you speak into.

clue.text: Barker must be a go-getter

definitions.meaning: a dog, here a gun dog breed
literally one who goes and fetches

explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gun dog that fetches game; read literally, someone who fetches things back.

clue.text: Conspirator who charts the course of an aircraft

definitions.text: who charts the course of an aircraft
definitions.meaning: a navigator or radar operator marking a flight's path

explanation.definitionFit: A schemer hatches a plot; a navigator plots a flight path on a chart.

clue.text: A toady contrived to plead

indicators.note: contrived means artfully arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sycophant devises a plea for favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A toady' looks like a flatterer, but it means something that becomes a toad: a frog-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of a frog or toad later grows into the adult amphibian.

clue.text: Reformationist peer holding everyone back

indicators.note: the peer holds the other piece within him, so it goes inside

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

indicators.note: back says the word for everyone is written from its end to its start

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A nobleman of the Reformation era restrains the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA, and 'holding' puts that inside LORD. The Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe, forerunners of the Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Wycliffe were early English religious reformers, ahead of the Protestant Reformation.

clue.text: Having fainted away with a common ailment

parts.note: out means away, as in 'she is out'
the common cold is the commonest ailment

explanation.surface: Someone has collapsed while suffering from a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' looks like part of the definition but belongs with ailment, describing the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knocked unconscious, as a boxer floored, is the state of having lost consciousness.

clue.text: Invite lag to be reformed guardian against crime

indicators.note: reformed means shaped anew, so the letters of the fodder are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old convict is asked along to go straight and help prevent crime.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lag' is British slang for a convict, so 'reformed' reads as going straight, but it signals rearranging INVITELAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-appointed citizen who punishes wrongdoers acts as a guard against lawbreaking.

clue.text: Rex enters into a brief presentation

indicators.note: one piece enters, going inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Rex, Latin for king, as in royal signatures

explanation.surface: A king walks into a short introductory talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A short opening to a song or speech is the informal, clipped form of introduction.

clue.text: See nothing but a film on tape

parts.note: vide is Latin for see, used in references
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: You get to view nothing except a recorded movie.
explanation.walkthrough: VIDE ('see') is used in notes to direct the reader elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A recording of moving pictures on magnetic cassette is exactly what a VHS recording was.

clue.text: At risk when telephoning

explanation.definitionFit: Something staked is in danger; someone on a call is connected by phone wire.

clue.text: Backing free rein given to poetry

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them fall into a new order

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A rider loosens the reins and turns to writing verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges REIN to INRE; 'given to' simply joins it to VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving backwards, as a car does when reversing, is going backwards.

clue.text: Post 1 to the Queen Mother?

definitions.meaning: one item of post addressed to a royal would be regal correspondence

explanation.definitionFit: Britain's postal service; also, whimsically, letters sent to a member of the royal family.

clue.text: Sounds like what ramblers are demanding immediately

indicators.note: says the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a near-twin spelling

parts.note: walkers campaign for a right of way, the legal right to cross land on a path

explanation.surface: Walkers want something, and they want it now.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'right of way' slurs to 'right o' way'. A right of way is a public footpath across private land, which British ramblers' groups defend.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at once or without delay is doing it instantly.

clue.text: How phone girl can show her number 18 no longer engaged!

definitions.text: How phone girl can show her number 18 no longer engaged!

parts.words: How phone girl can show her number 18 no longer engaged!
parts.note: a girl on the phone ends a call by hanging up; a girl whose betrothal is broken takes her engagement band from her finger

explanation.surface: A telephonist ends a call; a fiancee throws back her engagement token.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' plays on a phone line being busy and a couple being betrothed; the 18 refers to 18 down, an angry state.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a phone call by hanging up; jokingly, a broken engagement means removing the band.

clue.text: Became angry when old twig was broken

indicators.note: broken means snapped into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper when a dry stick snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing one's temper is flying into a furious rage.

clue.text: Equestrian condition

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a contract or verdict as a proviso

explanation.definitionFit: A horseman sits on a horse; an added clause qualifying an agreement is also called this.

clue.text: See cod I see sliced up

indicators.note: sliced up means cut into bits, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watching a fish being filleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not 'look': a bishop's see is his district.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the area under his church jurisdiction.

clue.text: What an army beats when it is beaten

definitions.text: What an army beats when it is beaten

parts.words: What an army beats when it is beaten
parts.note: a defeated army 'beats' a withdrawal, playing on the drum signal and the sense of losing

explanation.surface: An army sounds a drum signal after defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A withdrawal from battle is what defeated troops make, and to 'beat' one is the idiom.

clue.text: Saltpetre can upset sappers

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can
RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: Saltpetre explosive may knock over a tin held by army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TIN into NIT. The Royal Engineers (RE) are Britain's army engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, used in gunpowder, is known by this older chemical name.

clue.text: Resigned to the ultimate fate of a decayed tooth?

definitions.meaning: withdrew, quit a post or contest

definitions.text: the ultimate fate of a decayed tooth?
definitions.meaning: a rotten tooth ends up extracted by the dentist

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their job, as a bad tooth finally gives up its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to withdraw; a dentist finally extracts a rotten molar.

clue.text: Urge to get newspapers

definitions.meaning: to push someone hard to act

explanation.definitionFit: To push hard is to insist; journalism collectively is called the printed media.

clue.text: One is disposed to produce fluorescent dye

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to make a glowing colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A red dye used in laboratory staining glows under light.

clue.text: Green mineral oil refined by grape supplier

indicators.note: refined means processed into another form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a vine is the plant that bears grapes

explanation.surface: A winegrower produces processed oil of a greenish hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges OIL to OLI, and 'by' just sets it beside VINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is the gem form of this olive-green silicate rock-forming mineral.

clue.text: Stern and sober before going to Australia

indicators.note: one piece goes to the other, so the word for before follows the other piece

parts.note: Aust is a standard abbreviation for Australia
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A serious, teetotal person is emigrating to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' puts ERE (old 'before') after AUST, the abbreviation of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and plain in manner, without luxury or levity, describes a strict, unsmiling character.

clue.text: If upset a great number gets a fit of restlessness

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the two letters are swapped round

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated when a huge crowd is disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IF into FI; D is 500 in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Having 'the fidgets' means suffering a bout of nervous inability to keep still.

clue.text: Let about nine mess around, because too forgiving

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word Let goes round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to mess something around is to jumble it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Allowing nine people to fool about, because you go easy on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess around' turns NINE into NIEN, and 'about' wraps LET round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively soft or permissive treatment of wrongdoing is a merciful, indulgent attitude.
